uslaw-usc-t2-s135b:
Section 135b of Title 2 of the United States Code sets up local centers for blind readers. The Librarian of Congress may deal with libraries and groups to run them. Public libraries and non-profit groups may serve as the centers. They pass round the books, recordings, and players named in section 135a.

Music scores and teaching texts from a linked section are in the flow too. The centers work under terms and rules the Librarian lays down. First call on loans goes to set needs at all times. Blind folk and other handicapped folk who served with honour come first. Funds may be granted by Congress to carry the work out in full.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1905b:
Section 1905b of Title 2 of the United States Code requires notice before the Capitol Police commit certain funds. It sits in Chapter 29 of Title 2, on the Capitol Police, current through Public Law 119-134.

Beginning on March 15, 2022, the Chief of the United States Capitol Police must give written notice to two committees. They are the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives. The notice comes before any commitment of funds under section 1905 of the title that equals or exceeds 100,000 dollars. The section applies for fiscal year 2022 and each year after it.
uslaw-usc-t2-s195b:
Section 195b of Title 2 of the United States Code sets fees for witnesses asked to appear before the Senate Majority or Minority Policy Committee. It sits in Chapter 6 of Title 2, on congressional procedure and investigations, current through Public Law 119-134. The provision is a single sentence on pay and travel costs.

Any witness asked to appear before either committee is entitled to a witness fee for each full day spent travelling to and from the place of appearance. The witness also gets back actual and necessary travel costs for the trip. Both the fee and the costs are capped. They may not exceed the rates paid to witnesses appearing before committees of the Senate.
uslaw-usc-t2-s285b:
Section 285b of Title 2 lists the functions of the Office of Law Revision Counsel. The first function is revision of the statute book, one title at a time. The Office must prepare and submit to the House Judiciary Committee a complete compilation, restatement, and revision of the general and permanent laws.

The revision must conform to the understood policy, intent, and purpose of Congress in the original enactments. Amendments and corrections are allowed to remove ambiguities, contradictions, and other imperfections of substance and form, separately stated. The aim is the enactment of each title as positive law. The second function is a periodic review of all public laws, with recommendations to repeal provisions that are obsolete, superfluous, or superseded. The third is to prepare and publish new editions of the United States Code, with annual cumulative supplements. The section sits in Chapter 9A of Title 2.
